title: Estimating Treatment Effects on Disease Persistence from Rare State-Dependent Registry Visits
banked_reason: D0.5.G: tier=subfield < floor=field and not salvageable in scope; uniform LAN bound false, priority unresolved, finite-information transfer overclaimed.
gap_reasons: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR (triage, round 0) — D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope, so the directed-revise loop was stopped before spending its budget on a note that cannot clear the bar.

The asserted uniform score bound (6), used for (19)--(20), is false: with a one-mark channel β=√(αD), the passive zero-count log likelihood has ∂_r^3 log P(N=0)=Θ(ε_n^2D), not O(ε_n^2D^2); deterministic zero/singleton curvature must be cancelled explicitly or a joint-rate condition supplied before the no-extra-restriction LAN/Wald claim follows.

The central frontier's claimed separation from the closest classical MMPP asymptotics remains conditional on inaccessible Rydén (1994, 1995) theorem text; verify and compare that scope before presenting the rate/LAN package as theorem-level novel.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a matched minimax scale and baseline-assessment crossover for a known-channel stationary binary model, but the field-tier review stopped before formalization. The claimed uniform LAN/Wald proof relies on a false score bound, the finite-information argument does not establish uniform experiment transfer, and the closest classical MMPP priority comparison is incomplete. These issues must be resolved before the result is treated as a sound subfield theorem package.
tldr: A treatment can alter the persistence of a stationary binary disease while leaving prevalence unchanged. In a prospective randomized registry observed through rare state-dependent marked visits, the proposed theorem characterizes the effective information scale for this persistence contrast as \(n(\epsilon_n^2D_{a,n}^2+p_n\epsilon_nD_{a,n})\) in each arm, gives an exact-factorial-moment initializer and efficient exact-score estimator, proves a uniform local asymptotic normal experiment and matching minimax risk, and locates the one-baseline allocation crossover at \(p_n\asymp\epsilon_nD_{a,n}\). At bounded effective information, the scalar limit \(nv_{a,n}\to\lambda_a\) does not identify a unique experiment; after resolving passive-pair and baseline-singleton intensities, the boundary experiment is an explicit product marked-Poisson experiment, and the pure-channel limits are nonequivalent.
gap: Marked MMPP likelihoods and weak-emission HMM minimax theory exist separately. The inspected literature does not give a fixed-window triangular-array theorem in which visit intensity, marked-intensity separation, and an exact-baseline fraction can vanish together, and classical MMPP full-text priority remains only partially verifiable.
fill: The project derives uniform exact-likelihood information, exact unbiased factorial equations, an attaining one-step estimator, LAN and Wald inference, a matching Hellinger minimax lower bound, and the baseline crossover, while explicitly excluding visit-triggered enrollment and unconstrained scheduling claims.
